//: Type checking for the browser code.
checkJs is ON for assets/, engine/ and shared/. Files that are not type-clean
yet carry a `// @ts-nocheck` marker at the top of the file — that marker IS the
debt register, and removing one is the unit of work. Keeping it in the file
beats a list in this config for two reasons: it is visible to whoever opens the
file, and it survives a rename.
It also solves a problem `exclude` cannot: tsc follows imports regardless of
exclude, so one un-typed file in an import graph re-contaminates every clean
file that imports it. @ts-nocheck silences the file wherever it is reached from.
Run: npm run typecheck   (wired into npm run validate)
Most failures are one of these, and each is fixed at the lookup, not by
window.X unknown              -> declare X in types/globals.d.ts
